name: TyphoonSat
description: Abstract Tropical cyclones (TCs) in the Northwest Pacific pose significant threats to coastal regions, yet the lack of a standardized object-detection dataset hinders fair algorithm evaluation. We present TyphoonSat, a high-resolution satellite imagery dataset for TC detection spanning 2015–2024. It comprises 5390 Himawari-8/9 infrared cloud images (1601 × 1201 pixels, 5 km resolution) covering 100°E–180°E and 0°–60°N, with 7895 bounding-box annotations in YOLO format, derived from best-track records from the China Meteorological Administration (CMABST). The dataset supports coarse (all intensities regarded as one category) and fine-grained (six intensity levels) detection tasks. Benchmarks using YOLOv8 variants demonstrate strong performance for coarse detection (mAP@50 up to 0.923, CSI up to 0.791) and highlight challenges in distinguishing weak-to-moderate intensities, while SuperTY detection excels (CSI up to 0.609). This dataset provides a unified benchmark for TC detection and fosters advances in deep-learning-based meteorological remote sensing.
